questions.stem: The best method for obtaining pure water from muddy river water is
questions.explanation: Distillation boils the water off, leaving behind suspended mud and every dissolved salt, then condenses the pure vapour back to liquid. Filtration alone would remove the visible mud but leave all the dissolved impurities in the water.

distractorRationale.a: Filtration removes only insoluble suspended matter; dissolved salts pass straight through the paper
distractorRationale.c: Chromatography separates small quantities of soluble substances for analysis, not bulk purification
distractorRationale.d: Nothing in muddy water is magnetic

questions.stem: In filtration, the insoluble solid left on the filter paper is called the
questions.explanation: The residue is the solid retained by the filter paper because its particles are too large to pass through the pores. The clear liquid that passes through is the filtrate.

distractorRationale.a: The filtrate is the liquid that passes through, not the solid retained
distractorRationale.c: A distillate is the liquid collected after condensation in distillation
distractorRationale.d: A sublimate is the solid re-formed after a substance has sublimed

questions.stem: Ethanol boils at 78 degrees Celsius and water at 100 degrees Celsius. The two liquids are completely miscible. The most suitable method of separating them is
questions.explanation: The two boiling points differ by only 22 degrees, so vapour leaving the flask in simple distillation would contain a good deal of water. A fractionating column provides many condensation and re-evaporation cycles, each one enriching the vapour in the more volatile ethanol, so a much purer distillate is collected.

distractorRationale.a: A separating funnel only works for immiscible liquids that form two layers, and these two mix completely
distractorRationale.b: Simple distillation is adequate only when boiling points differ widely, roughly by more than 25 to 30 degrees

questions.stem: In a paper chromatography experiment a coloured spot travels 3.6 cm while the solvent front travels 8.0 cm. Calculate the Rf value of the spot, giving your answer to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: Rf is the distance moved by the spot divided by the distance moved by the solvent front, so Rf = 3.6 / 8.0 = 0.45. Because it is a ratio of two lengths it has no unit, and it must always come out between 0 and 1.

questions.stem: A mixture contains sodium chloride, sand and ammonium chloride. Which sequence separates all three?

options.text: Sublime, then dissolve in water and filter, then crystallise the filtrate
Dissolve in water, then use a separating funnel, then sublime
Use a magnet, then filter, then distil

questions.explanation: Ammonium chloride is the only component that sublimes, so gentle heating removes it first and it is collected on a cool surface. Adding water then dissolves the sodium chloride but not the sand, so filtration gives sand as residue. Evaporating and cooling the filtrate crystallises the sodium chloride.

distractorRationale.a: Filtering the dry solid mixture achieves nothing because there is no liquid, and it never separates the two soluble solids
distractorRationale.c: A separating funnel is for immiscible liquids, and dissolving first would put both salts into the same solution
distractorRationale.d: None of the three components is magnetic

questions.stem: During distillation the bulb of the thermometer must be placed level with the side arm of the flask because

options.text: it prevents the liquid from bumping
it measures the temperature of the vapour passing into the condenser
it stops heat escaping from the flask
it speeds up condensation in the Liebig condenser

questions.explanation: The reading that matters is the boiling point of the substance actually distilling over, and that is the temperature of the vapour just as it leaves for the condenser. If the bulb dips into the liquid or sits too high, the reading will not be the true boiling point of the distillate.

distractorRationale.a: Bumping is prevented by adding anti-bumping granules, not by thermometer position
distractorRationale.c: The thermometer plays no part in insulating the flask
distractorRationale.d: Condensation rate depends on the cooling water, not on where the thermometer sits

questions.stem: The baseline in paper chromatography should be drawn in ink so that it is clearly visible.
questions.explanation: False. The baseline must be drawn in pencil. Ink contains soluble dyes that would dissolve in the solvent and run up the paper, contaminating the chromatogram. Pencil graphite is insoluble and stays where it is drawn.
